sentences.text: Comahuesaurus is a genus of sauropod dinosaur belonging to the family Rebbachisauridae.
The holotype, which is the single specimen the species is based on, consists of a neural arch from a lower-back vertebra.

However, abundant material from at least three individuals includes thirty-seven tail vertebrae, partial back vertebrae, a breastbone, a shoulder blade, a complete upper arm bone, a hip bone, a complete thigh bone, and leg bones.
The upper arm bone measures 67.5 cm in length, while the thigh bone measures 113 cm.
The type species, C. windhauseni, was named in honor of Anselmo Windhausen for his contributions to the geological study of Patagonia.
Fossil remains belonging to at least three individuals were found in the Lohan Cura Formation in southern Neuquén Province, Argentina.
The bonebed preserving these remains is believed to have been deposited rapidly by a single catastrophic event, likely a flash flood from an ephemeral river.
Comahuesaurus possessed a reduced hyposphene-hypantrum system, a trait shared with more derived rebbachisaurids but not yet fully lost in this species.
This animal lived during the Early Cretaceous, specifically from the Aptian to Albian stages, in the Lohan Cura Formation of Argentina.
Its existence spanned from 119.57 to 110.1 million years ago.
